Hi Elaine,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a short proposal for the latency SLOs we discussed for FinOptics (p50/p95) along with an operational runbook sketch for measurement and evidence collection. TL;DR: we propose a weighted sliding-window approach to avoid long-tail masking while still smoothing transient noise.

Key bullets:
- Targets: p50 = 45 ms, p95 = 280 ms (applies to your primary inference route /v1/generate).
- Measurement window: 30-day sliding window composed of 1-hour buckets; final percentiles computed using an exponential weighting that emphasizes the most recent 72 hours.
- Carveouts: planned deploy windows and scheduled maintenance (customer-notified) are excluded; transient spikes from upstream network outages have an automated detection and provisional carveout path.
- Credits: proposed credit matrix in the attached PDF (tiered by outage duration and severity).

I've CC'd Kimberly (legal/pricing) and Aditya (runtime product) for any commercial or technical detail that needs to be tightened. Two asks for you: (1) confirm the route(s) in scope (I had /v1/generate as primary + embeddings as optional), and (2) let me know procurement timing so we can align the DocuSign.

Attachment: redwood-weighted-slo-proposal-v1.pdf (3 pages)

Best,
Marcus Lin

Elaine — appreciate the quick review. Short answers up front, then technical detail below.

Short answers:
- Exponential weighting is deterministic and computed from raw 1-hour buckets; we will include the exact formula in the contract addendum and provide the code snippet used to compute the weighted quantiles for audit.
- Deploy carveouts: rolling deploys that increase error/latency by > 30% in 5 consecutive buckets will be flagged; if customer and Redwood both confirm it's a deploy, we can provisionally carve it out pending post-mortem within 72 hours. Planned maintenance windows (notified 48+ hours ahead) are automatically excluded.
- Evidence: we will provide hourly percentile buckets (raw) for 90 days via secure S3 export + request-level traces for incidents (sampled, full traces for flagged incidents) for 365 days. Export format: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) and CSV.

Technical detail (for your SRE):
- Measurement pipeline: each inference request records route, region, model variant, and latency (us). Latencies aggregated into fixed 1-hour buckets (UTC).
- Weighted aggregation: given N hourly buckets b_1..b_N with bucket timestamps t_1..t_N (t_N most recent), weight w_i = exp(-(t_N - t_i) / half_life), where half_life = 72 hours. Weighted quantile algorithm uses linear interpolation on the weighted empirical CDF. We'll append the code reference in the runbook.
- Window length: 30 days (sliding) but we also publish a 7-day short window for operational visibility. The legal SLO uses the 30-day weighted result.
- Per-route SLOs: p50/p95 computed per route and per-region (you can opt-in to consolidated cross-region SLOs if desired).
- Canary behavior: canary failures are isolated and do not automatically impact production SLOs unless the canary is promoted.

I'll ask Rishi to attach a one-page runbook cover that lists the operational hooks, on-call escalation (primary: infra-oncall@redwood.ai, backup: svc-ops@redwood.ai), and a checklist for evidence exports.

If that aligns, Kimberly will draft the contract language for credits and caps.

Best,
Marcus
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Weighted-window p50/p95 proposal — commercial language draft

Marcus/Aditya/Rishi — drafting notes for the legal addendum and pricing team. Please comment inline. Proposed contract language (high level):

- Definitions: SLO measurement uses the 30-day weighted sliding window described in the Measurement Runbook; weighting formula (half-life = 72h) included as deterministic algorithmic appendix.
- Credits: if monthly weighted p95 for an in-scope route exceeds the committed threshold, Redwood issues credits equal to 5% of the monthly committed spend for first breach, 10% for second within a rolling 90-day period. Cap: credits not to exceed 50% of the affected month's committed spend.
- Evidence & auditability: Redwood will deliver hourly percentile buckets (1h windows) for 90 days and incident traces for 365 days; customer may request a one-time audit export in a mutually agreed format.
- Carveouts: planned maintenance windows (48+ hour notice), confirmed provider-initiated infra failures, and mutually confirmed deploy incidents are eligible for carveout; carveouts must be requested and documented within 7 days of the incident.
- Termination/exit: if repeated SLA failures (3 breaches in a rolling 180-day window) cause material business impact, customer has right to terminate with 30 days notice and prorated refund per existing commitments.

Open items for pricing/legal: whether to use fixed credit % above or a linear function tied to minutes out of SLO. Also need to confirm if FinOptics requires SOC2-level cross-checks on the measurement pipeline logs (they often do).

I'll prepare a redline for the addendum and loop in legal if needed.

Kimberly Park
Head of Pricing & Contracts — Redwood Inference
